claims.text: Setting the PULUMI_TFE_DOMAIN environment variable on the self-hosted Pulumi Cloud API service lets Terraform and OpenTofu use the self-hosted Pulumi Cloud as a state backend.
The PULUMI_TFE_DOMAIN environment variable specifies the domain that serves the Terraform-compatible API on the self-hosted Pulumi Cloud API service.
When the PULUMI_TFE_DOMAIN environment variable is unset, the Terraform-compatible API on the self-hosted Pulumi Cloud API service is disabled and its routes are not registered.
The DNS record for the PULUMI_TFE_DOMAIN domain should point at the same host that serves the PULUMI_API_DOMAIN.

Using a separate domain for PULUMI_TFE_DOMAIN keeps the Terraform-compatible API distinct from the Pulumi API, but a separate domain is not required, since PULUMI_TFE_DOMAIN can be set to the same value as PULUMI_API_DOMAIN.

In Terraform or OpenTofu configuration, in the `terraform login` or `tofu login` command, and in the `TF_TOKEN_*` variable name, the PULUMI_TFE_DOMAIN value should be used wherever the state backend guide (/docs/integrations/terraform/state-backend/) uses `tf.pulumi.com`.
The Pulumi documentation's state backend guide is located at /docs/integrations/terraform/state-backend/.
